summary.short: Binding code made by Coimisiún na Meán under the Online Safety and Media Regulation Act 2022 for designated video-sharing platform services in Ireland. It requires restriction of harmful videos and commercial communications, age assurance, parental controls and complaint handling; Part B applies from a date the Commission sets.
summary.long: Code adopted under the Online Safety and Media Regulation Act 2022 and Article 28b of the Audiovisual Media Services Directive. Part A (sections 1 to 10) sets scope and general duties: it applies to video-sharing platform services designated under Irish jurisdiction, requires appropriate measures to protect children and the general public, and states that age verification based solely on self-declaration is not effective. Non-compliance is a contravention under Part 8B of the Act, and providers must maintain systems and controls to demonstrate compliance; the Commission considers size and nature of the service. Part B (sections 11 to 17), applying from a date set by the Commission, requires platforms' terms to restrict harmful video and commercial communications, adult-only content access controls and content rating, account suspension after prior warning, parental controls where users under 16 are permitted, reporting and flagging, complaint procedures, an annual media literacy action plan, a ban on commercial processing of children's personal data, and reports to the Commission every 3 months. The Code states no fine amounts.

notes: The Code applies to named video-sharing platform services designated by the Commission (section 2.3), but the document names none; the register is external (footnote 1). Part B (sections 11 to 17) applies from a date the Commission will determine, and no date is stated in the text. Section 1.5 states that the whole Code is binding and applies to all such services, while sections 9.2 and 10.8 allow the Commission to take account of service size and nature. Section 11 defines child as under 18, while section 14.1 sets an under-16 threshold for parental controls. Footnote 3 states that self-declaration of age is not an effective age assurance measure for Part A, and section 12.10 says the same for Part B. The adoption date is not stated in the text. Foreword references to the EU Terrorist Content Online Regulation and to An Garda Síochána are context only and are not cited in operative provisions.
